contentChunks.htmlValue: Usage

A FAB menu opens from a FAB to show multiple related actions. It should always appear in the same place as the FAB that opened it.

This makes actions immediately accessible, and keeps the UI clean by concealing actions when they’re not needed.

Don’t open a FAB menu from an extended FAB or any other component.

contentChunks.footer: The FAB menu should always open from a FAB
contentChunks.altText: 1 mobile screen with a FAB, 1 with a FAB menu. Both are right aligned.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
The FAB menu should be aligned to the trailing edge of the window. 

In right-to-left (RTL) languages, this means the FAB and FAB menu should be aligned to the left edge, and the layout of elements should be mirrored.

contentChunks.footer: In RTL languages, the FAB menu should be left-aligned with the icon and text placement mirrored
contentChunks.altText: 1 mobile screen with a FAB, 1 with a FAB menu. Both are left aligned and mirrored for a right-to-left language.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
FAB menus can contain 2–6 items. These should be closely related under a single action, like Share. 

Avoid grouping unrelated actions in the same FAB menu.

contentChunks.footer: FAB menus can have 2-6 items
contentChunks.altText: A FAB menu with 5 options on a photo gallery UI.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t use a FAB menu with one item
contentChunks.altText: A FAB menu with 1 option on a photo gallery UI.

contentChunks.htmlValue: When a FAB is paired with other components, like the floating toolbar or navigation rail, don’t use the FAB menu. This prevents cognitive overload and interface clutter.

contentChunks.footer: FABs can be placed next to toolbars and other components
contentChunks.altText: A toolbar with a FAB directly next to it.

contentChunks.footer: Don't use a FAB menu with a toolbar or navigation rail
contentChunks.altText: A toolbar with a FAB menu next to it.

contentChunks.htmlValue: FAB menu items should always have label text. The icons shouldn’t be removed since they make each item easy to identify.

contentChunks.footer: Only remove the icon if necessary. The icon provides a differentiation between items.

contentChunks.htmlValue: The list item should always hug its contents and look consistent. Avoid truncating text or setting fixed widths. All FAB menu elements should be rounded.

contentChunks.footer: Keep the padding between the container and icon, icon and text, and text and container consistent
contentChunks.altText: A FAB menu used out of the box with no configurations.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t expand container sizes

contentChunks.htmlValue: Adaptive layout
The FAB menu can open from any sized FAB. Use with a FAB size suitable for the window size class. For example, larger FABs are recommended for larger windows.

contentChunks.footer: The FAB menu works in any window size. Pair it with the FAB suitable for that window size.
contentChunks.altText: The same FAB menu used in medium and compact window sizes.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
The FAB menu should remain anchored to the same corner or edge regardless of window size. 

In large and extra large windows, the FAB and FAB menu margins should increase from 16dp to 24dp.

contentChunks.footer: On desktop, use larger FABs and margins
contentChunks.altText: A FAB menu with 24dp margins from the edge of the window.

contentChunks.htmlValue: On web, the FAB menu uses a menu component for an experience that's consistent with other desktop apps.

contentChunks.footer: The same FAB menu options on both large window (left) and an Android compact window (right)
contentChunks.altText: A FAB menu using menu component on web and traditional FAB menu on compact screen.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Behavior

Appearing

The FAB should transform into the close button of the FAB menu. The menu items should appear using the enter and exit transition.

Originate the transition from one of the FAB's trailing corners, preferably the top-aligned corner.

contentChunks.footer: Animate FAB menus from the top-aligned corner of FABs
contentChunks.altText: A FAB transforms into a FAB menu while anchoring the animation to the top right corner of the FAB.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
To ensure accessibility for keyboard users on the web, avoid positioning the FAB menu to completely obscure the focus indicator of an actionable element. 

Partially covering the desired element is fine, as long as the focus indicator is visible.

contentChunks.footer: Ensure the actionable element and its focus indicator are visible behind the FAB menu
contentChunks.altText: FAB menu doesn’t obscure actionable element and its focus indicator.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t block an actionable element and its focus indicator completely with the FAB menu
contentChunks.altText: FAB menu obscures both an actionable element and its focus indicator.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Scrolling

When window height is limited, like when viewing phones in horizontal orientation, FAB menu items can scroll. 

The items should scroll behind the close button.

contentChunks.footer: FAB menus can scroll if the window height is too short to contain all the options
contentChunks.altText: A FAB menu with 6 items scrolls off screen on a horizontal-oriented device. Scrolled items move behind the close button.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Expanding

Any FAB menu item can expand and adapt to any shape using a container transform transition pattern. This includes a surface that is part of the app structure, or a surface that spans the entire screen.

contentChunks.footer: FAB menu items can transition into any kind of shape when selected
contentChunks.altText: A FAB menu item expands and transforms into a full screen dialog.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Use cases

People should be able to do the following using assistive technology:

  • Navigate and interact with the FAB menu
  • Ensure focus is correct when navigating through the menu
Interaction & style
FAB menu elements meet the minimum target size of 48dp.

contentChunks.footer: FAB menus have 48x48dp minimum width and sufficient spacing by default
contentChunks.altText: FAB menu measurement annotations. All elements are larger than the minimum target size.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
When the FAB menu can scroll, make sure the items scroll behind the close button. 

The close button should always be easy to access and unobstructed.

contentChunks.footer: Allow the menu items to scroll behind the close button
contentChunks.altText: FAB menu items are scrolling behind the close button.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t obstruct the close button in short screens like horizontal orientation
contentChunks.altText: FAB menu items are scrolling in front of the close button.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Initial focus

When the FAB is selected, the FAB menu opens, and initial focus remains on the close button, which takes the place of the original FAB.

Then the focus moves from the top menu item to the bottom.

contentChunks.footer:
Focus lands on the close button. People can then navigate through all the items.

  1. Close button
  2. First menu item
  3. Second menu item
  4. Third menu item
contentChunks.altText: 4 FAB menus with the focus order labelled. Focus moves from the close button at the bottom to the topmost menu item next.

Keys

Actions

Labeling elements

Android

On Android, a FAB menu’s close button should include a state to tell screen readers what action will occur when it's toggled. The close button should be labeled: 

  • Label: Toggle menu

  • Role: Button

  • State: Expanded or collapsed

contentChunks.footer: On Android, the close button accessibility labels should include a toggle menu label, button role, and an expanded or collapsed state
contentChunks.altText: Accessibility labels for the close button on an Android device.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
FAB menu items should be labeled:

  • Label: Match the item’s UI text, such as Reply all 

  • Role: Button

contentChunks.footer: Label FAB menu items to match their UI text, like Reply all, and use the button role
contentChunks.altText: Accessibility labels for a FAB menu item on an Android device.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Web

On web, a FAB menu is a combination of a FAB and a menu component. The FAB opens the menu. Follow the accessibility guidelines for FABs and menus.

The FAB's accessibility label should describe the menu that the FAB will open.
